Each of its 10 triads gets one of 16 types; the table lists the non-zero counts with the triads behind them: 2 each of 012, 102, 021U, and 021C, 1 cyclic triad 030C (C, D, E, accent color), and 1 120U (A, B, C, teal). Every other type is 0." width="100%"} A triad is any set of three nodes. In a directed graph each pair of them is connected mutually, one way, or not at all, giving 16 possible triad types (up to isomorphism). The triadic census counts how many of each the graph contains, and is a classic fingerprint of social structure (Holland & Leinhardt, 1976): transitive triads (`030T`) signal hierarchy, cyclic ones (`030C`) the absence of rank, mutual pairs (`102`, `201`, `300`) reciprocity, and so on. Comparing the census with random graphs of the same size and density shows which patterns are over-represented. Types use the standard MAN labels: the digits count **M**utual, **A**symmetric and **N**ull pairs, and a letter tells apart types with the same counts (**D**own, **U**p, **C**yclic, **T**ransitive), e.g. `021D` is one node pointing at both others. The counts always add up to `n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) / 6`. Parallel edges count once and self-loops are ignored. The algorithm (Batagelj & Mrvar, 2001) only visits connected triads, so it scales to large sparse graphs. Results match NetworkX's `triadic_census()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[str, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The count of each of the 16 triad types, keyed by MAN label, in the standard order `003, 012, 102, 021D, 021U, 021C, 111D, 111U, 030T, 030C, 201, 120D, 120U, 120C, 210, 300`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A three-node cycle is a single cyclic triad; reversing one edge makes it transitive: ::: {#232fdcb8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec cycle = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) cycle.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) flow = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) flow.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("A", "C")]) cycle.triadic_census()["030C"], flow.triadic_census()["030T"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1, 1) ``` ::: ::: On a larger network, the non-empty types tell the story at a glance: ::: {#477fba7b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "A"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "C")]) {k: v for k, v in graph.triadic_census().items() if v} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'012': 2, '102': 2, '021U': 2, '021C': 2, '030C': 1, '120U': 1} ``` ::: :::
